thread:
jane_sales: Quick heads-up — AcmeHealth POC wants Redwood Private in their VPC. They want no internet egress from the data plane, and prefer an interface endpoint (VPCE) over peering. Also asking if we can hand them a scoped hosted API key for the POC and a dedicated pool reserved for the trial.
alex_sre: ok. two parts: control plane access (hosted API key) + data plane connectivity (VPCE or peering). If they want no internet egress, VPCE interface endpoint + PrivateLink to our service is the safer option.
sam_security: Please confirm compliance checklist: private DNS, HGW/NAT disabled, and KMS CMKs for logs. Also require rotation window for POC keys (7d?) and audit logging.
jane_sales: they asked for 7-day key rotation — ok to recommend 7d. Pricing question: want to know if a small dedicated pool (2xA10G) can be trialed with hourly billing. Can we do that short-term?
morgan_eng: for Dedicated pools we can do short-term reserved capacity for POC — we'll need to allocate slices in the pool and tag them. Ops can toggle billing to hourly for internal tracking, but sales needs to OK a one-off credit adjustment.
eric_se: networking checklist I recommend sending them: 1) Create interface endpoint in their subnet (private IP), 2) Add route table to point to TGW or local routes as appropriate, 3) Create Private Hosted Zone in their account and map 'api.redwood-private.' to the VPCE DNS, 4) Provide list of source IPs for allowlist if they insist on IP-level.
jane_sales: can you paste a minimal route table example? customer uses shared services TGW and has restrictions on route propagation.
morgan_eng: sure — paste below:
```
# Example: route table for subnets hosting VPCE
Destination     Target
10.0.0.0/16     local
0.0.0.0/0       igw (NOT used for private-only setup)
10.100.0.0/16   tgw-attach
```
Notes: with interface endpoints you don't need a route for the service itself, but you must ensure the subnet has connectivity to our regional endpoint via the interface endpoint.
alex_sre: If they can't modify TGW policies, peering might be simpler but peering is transitive only with TGW; otherwise you need explicit routes. PrivateLink avoids cross-account route changes and gives more isolation. Also watch for DNS: enable 'Private DNS' on the VPCE if they want transparent hostnames.
sam_security: also confirm we can support SAML-backed console for their team? they want limited console access to see usage. For POC, read-only should be fine.
eric_se: Hosted API key scope: create a role-scoped API key (scoped to project:acme-poc) + allowlist for key usage from their account VPCE if they supply the endpoint-id. We'll include short-lived tokens too for SDK usage.
jane_sales: awesome. Can we send them a one-pager with exact steps and a checklist? If you drop the checklist here I'll convert to a PPT.\almighty-deploy-bot: Provision request queued: POC_DED_POOL_acme_1749876543 — ETA 4h for pool carve.\morgan_eng: Checklist draft: 1) Confirm account IDs & VPC IDs, 2) Decide: PrivateLink (recommended) vs VPC Peering, 3) Create interface endpoint in chosen subnet(s) and enable Private DNS, 4) Share endpoint-id + VPC id with us for allowlist & routing checks, 5) Request hosted API key (we'll create scoped key + rotation policy), 6) Optional: request dedicated pool (ops ticket), 7) Validate TLS certs if they want mutual TLS, 8) Run smoke test with curl from their subnet using internal FQDN.
eric_se: Add: if they use split-horizon DNS, they must ensure resolution flows to the Private Hosted Zone in their account — otherwise hostnames will still leak to public.
jane_sales: perfect. I'll send this now and ask for account IDs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
